projects.title: AeroGuard: Intelligent Prognostics for Aerospace Propulsion Systems
projects.description: A Grand Unified pipeline that combines survival analysis, regime-aware normalization, fault isolation and ensemble regression to predict Remaining Useful Life (RUL) for turbofan engines using the NASA C-MAPSS datasets (FD001-FD004).
projects.long_description: AeroGuard was developed as the capstone for 'Programmation Statistique avec R'. It implements a four-phase approach: (1) survival analysis (Cox PH) to identify leading failure indicators, (2) regime detection and per-regime normalization to remove flight-condition noise (FD002), (3) unsupervised fault isolation and fault-aware models for multi-fault datasets (FD003), and (4) a unified pipeline that combines regime normalization + fault classification + ensemble regression for the combined FD004 dataset. The project includes data preprocessing, feature engineering (rolling-window statistics, regime-wise z-scoring, PCA health-index), model training (Random Forest, XGBoost), and production-ready artifacts (notebooks, saved models, and a final Quarto presentation).

phases.FD001: Baseline single-regime analysis. Cox PH used to identify sensor 11 (static pressure) as a dominant leading indicator; Random Forest regression produced RMSE 17.53.
phases.FD002: Multi-regime (altitude) challenge solved via K-Means regime detection and per-regime Z-score normalization; hybrid ensemble achieved RMSE ~26.5.
phases.FD003: Multi-fault dataset. Hierarchical clustering and fault-aware XGBoost regressors isolate failure modes (Fan vs Compressor) and produce RMSE ~20.0.
phases.FD004: Grand Unified pipeline combining regime normalization + fault classification + ensemble regression to generalize across regimes and faults; final RMSE reported ~32.97 after post-processing and physics-aware smoothing.

projects.title: Tennis & Padel Analysis
projects.description: Integrated AI system for automated tennis and padel match analysis combining deep learning, computer vision, and data science pipelines. Published and awarded Best Project of the Semester.
projects.long_description: Spearheaded an integrated AI system for automated tennis and padel match analysis combining deep learning, computer vision, and data science pipelines. Assembled a U-Net-based CNN (BallTrackerNet/TrackNet) for ball detection and trajectory tracking, achieving 95%+ accuracy. Redesigned CourtKeypointNet for court keypoint estimation and homography mapping, increasing keypoint accuracy by 8%. Utilized a pre-trained Faster R-CNN (ResNet50-FPN backbone) for player detection and tracking. Applied CatBoostRegressor for bounce detection and shot event classification. Leveraged OpenCV for frame processing and Albumentations for dataset augmentation. Computed advanced match analytics (heatmaps, positional density, player movement stats) using NumPy and Pandas. Developed and trained all models in Python (PyTorch) on CUDA-enabled GPUs, tested on both local and Google Colab environments. Spearheading development of a mobile application to provide real-time, on-court access to analytics.

introduction.greeting: Hello everyone, my name is Aymen Mabrouk. I'm a Software Engineer graduate, and I'm currently completing the final year of my Data Science Engineering degree at Polytechnique Sousse.
introduction.dual_degree_approach: I've been pursuing a double academic path in Software Engineering and Data Science, which has allowed me to combine solid development skills with advanced knowledge in AI and Machine Learning.
introduction.current_objective: This year, I'm looking for an end-of-studies internship (Projet de PFE) — an opportunity to apply what I've learned, work on real-world challenges, and continue growing as an engineer passionate about innovation and intelligent systems.

professional_journey.starting_point: I started my journey as a Full Stack Developer, learning algorithms, Java, and the basics of Python. Step by step, I built my foundation in software engineering, understanding how systems work, how to design them, and how to make them efficient.
professional_journey.evolution: But soon, I wanted to go beyond code — I wanted to make systems intelligent. That's when I dove deeper into Data Science and Artificial Intelligence, discovering how powerful data can be when combined with the right algorithms.
professional_journey.passion_discovery: Along the way, I became truly passionate about solving complex problems — the kind that require both creativity and logic — using Automation, Data Science, Machine Learning, and the latest Generative AI technologies.
professional_journey.mission_statement: My mission today is simple yet powerful: To transform code and data into intelligent solutions that deliver tangible business value.

foundation_years.achievement: Major of promotion, 18/20 grade, Très Bien mention
foundation_years.description: After obtaining my Baccalaureate in Science in 2020, during the year of the pandemic, I began my higher studies at ESST Hammam Sousse. There, I received a comprehensive education in Software Development, with a strong focus on Full-Stack Development and System Design.
foundation_years.technical_foundation: I worked on web, mobile, and IoT applications, which helped me understand how every layer of a system connects — from backend logic, to user interfaces, to connected devices.
foundation_years.capstone_project: During my final year, I completed an end-of-studies internship where I built a complete IoT system for server room monitoring, combining hardware sensors, web dashboards, and a mobile app. This project brought together everything I had learned — IoT, web, and mobile development — and earned an excellent grade of 18/20, a mention 'Très Bien', and was recognized as one of the best projects of the year.
foundation_years.graduation_honor: I also graduated as major of my promotion, which was a proud moment for me.

specialization_master.decision: After earning my degree, I received several offers — either to continue working where I did my internship or to continue my studies. I decided to pursue my academic journey and was accepted into multiple master's programs. I chose to join the Master's in Software Engineering at ISIM Monastir.
specialization_master.breakthrough: This is where I truly specialized. I focused on Advanced System Architecture and Data Management, but most importantly, this is where I discovered my passion for Applied Machine Learning and Computer Vision. I realized I excelled in Python and that my real interest wasn't just in building systems, but in making them think.

capstone_project.description: I built their entire AI-powered entry and exit system from the ground up. This was a complete, industrial-scale solution. It was a full-stack project with a web dashboard, a mobile app, and deep AI integration, using both Computer Vision for recognition and Generative AI for processing.
capstone_project.impact: It was a massive success with over 500 users. This project proved I could take all the advanced AI concepts and engineer them into a real, working, high-value product.

dual_degree_challenge.decision: After my first year at ISIM, I was accepted into Polytechnique Sousse for an Engineering degree in Data Science. So, I decided to challenge myself—by managing both degrees in parallel.
dual_degree_challenge.motivation: It was an intense year of dedication and organization, but my goal was clear: to fuse the robust architecture of software engineering with the specialized intelligence of data science.
dual_degree_challenge.parallel_achievement: So, at the exact same time I was doing all that AI research at Polytechnique, I was also completing my Master's in Software Engineering at ISIMM. It was a huge challenge, but I managed both concurrently and graduated from ISIMM with High Honors.
core_specializations: Deep Learning and Computer Vision - This is my core. I live in Python and PyTorch, and I love getting my hands dirty training and optimizing complex models.
Generative AI - I didn't just read about it; I started building with it, understanding how to apply LLMs to solve actual problems.
Integration and Implementation - For me, an AI model sitting on a laptop is useless. The real magic happens when you integrate it into a real system that people can use.

flagship_project.future_plan: This isn't just a research project; I'm now planning how to get this AI into a real mobile app for players to use.

professional_identity.technical_philosophy: Over the past few years, I've dedicated myself to mastering the intersection of robust software engineering and cutting-edge AI. My dual degree approach—Master's in Software Engineering plus Engineering in Data Science—gives me a rare hybrid skillset that companies actively seek.
professional_identity.growth_mindset: Every step of my journey has been about pushing boundaries: from building production-ready full-stack systems to architecting multi-agent RAG systems. I don't just study AI—I build intelligent systems that solve real problems and create tangible value.
professional_identity.value_proposition: I combine the robust architecture of software engineering with specialized AI expertise (LangChain, LangGraph, multi-agent systems) to create solutions that are not just innovative, but production-ready and business-valuable. I'm not a typical data scientist who only trains models, nor just a full-stack developer—I'm a builder who can design, implement, and deploy end-to-end AI-powered applications.
professional_identity.unique_positioning: My profile is deliberately rare: I can architect a React/Next.js frontend, build Node.js/FastAPI backends, design multi-agent RAG systems with LangChain/LangGraph, implement NLP pipelines, and deploy everything to production. This 'Full-Stack AI Engineer' positioning makes me valuable for projects that require both software engineering rigor and AI innovation.
